ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the two diagonals $AC, BD$ of the square $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$, and point $E$ is on $BD$, with $BE=BC$. What is the degree measure of $\angle ACE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In square $ABCD$, $\angle CBD=\angle ACB=45^\circ$,\\
$\because BE=BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCE=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-\angle CBD\right)=67.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACE=\angle BCE-\angle ACB=\boxed{22.5^\circ}$.

From the diagram, ABCD is a square with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right; diagonal BD runs from B to D and E lies on this diagonal, with segment CE drawn. Since BD is a diagonal of the square, it makes a 45° angle with side BC, so ∠CBE = 45°. The text gives BE = BC, so triangle BCE is isosceles with vertex angle 45° at B. Therefore each base angle, including ∠BCE, is (180° - 45°)/2 = 67.5°. Also diagonal AC of the square makes ∠BCA = 45°. Since ray CA lies inside ∠BCE in the diagram, ∠ACE = ∠BCE - ∠BCA = 67.5° - 45° = 22.5°.
